newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE CONSIDERS CUTBACK.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH PREMIER LEAGUE CONSIDERS CUTBACK.

text.p: English premier league officials are considering reducing the top flight competition from 20 clubs to 18, newspapers reported on Thursday.
Premier league chief executive Peter Leaver was quoted as saying the country's top sides may also withdraw from the League Cup in a bid to improve England's standing in Europe.
"We may have to do both eventually," Leaver said after a meeting of English clubs involved in Europe this season.
Several premier league coaches have blamed a congested domestic fixture calendar on England's poor performances in European club competition in recent years.
UEFA want England to have an 18-team competition to fall in line with most of the rest of Europe. This would allow for a further expansion of the European Cup, the Guardian said.
UEFA was considering reducing the number of English clubs allowed to compete in Europe if the premier league did not cut its numbers by two, the paper added.
